app.title: The Deepfake Detective Academy
app.hook: AI can do more every day. It can even speak in a voice you trust.

soundcheck.intro: Before we start: can you actually hear me? Everything after this is sound.
soundcheck.title: Sound check
soundcheck.body: Press the button. You should hear a short sentence. If it stays quiet, check the sound first.
soundcheck.tipsTitle: No sound? Try these, in this order
soundcheck.tip1: Turn the volume up on the device and in the browser.
soundcheck.tip2: Check the silent switch or Do Not Disturb; on a tablet it mutes everything.
soundcheck.tip3: If you're wearing headphones, check they're plugged in properly.
soundcheck.tip4: Press the test sound once more. Some browsers start audio after a tap.

setup.title: No audio samples yet
setup.body: The demo needs a set of audio samples first. Run these commands in the project folder:
setup.brokenTitle: The sample pack can't be read
setup.brokenBody: The manifest.json has an unexpected format. Regenerate the pack:

miko.name: Miko the minion
miko.description: Miko understands words well. A fake voice can still fool him.

echo.name: Agent Echo the detective
echo.description: Agent Echo hunts for the tiny sound clues that give a fake voice away.

b1.title: Inside the brain of a speech AI
b1.text: Hi, I'm Miko. I turn sound into words. See how it works.

b2.title: Real or Fake?
b2.text: Five voices. Which are human and which came from a computer? Look and listen closely.
b2.hintSpec: Read it from left to right. Look for rigid lines, empty gaps and a top edge that suddenly goes blank.
b2.hintAudio: Listen for breaths, small mistakes, odd pauses and a voice that sounds unusually smooth.

b3.title: The compression machine
b3.text: Phones and apps compress audio. See what happens to the details.

b4.title: The fake-voice factory
b4.text: AI can copy a familiar voice. Make a fake message and see who it fools.

b5.title: Clone your own voice
b5.text: Read aloud for ten seconds. This computer creates a new sentence in your voice, locally. Agent Echo hears only the result and makes its own guess.

station1.name: Inside the brain of a speech AI

stage0.miko: Sound is wobbling air! This is how a sentence feels in my ears. Press Listen.

stage1.miko: I turn sound into a picture. Low tones sit at the bottom, high tones at the top. Bright means loud. Find the loudest moment.

stage2.miko: Now I find small chunks of sound. I make a guess for each one.

stage3.miko: And then I glue the chunks together into words. Look, I'm writing along!

station1.waveLabel: The shape of the sound: tall means loud, flat means quiet
station1.specAlt: A sound picture: time runs left to right, low tones at the bottom, high tones at the top. Bright patches are loud.
station1.scrubLabel: Point at a moment in the sound picture
station1.scrubHint: Tap the picture, or use the arrow keys, to jump to that moment. Home and End go to the start and the end.
station1.peakPrompt: Point at the moment you think is the LOUDEST, then confirm.
station1.peakClose: Spot on. The loudest moment is around {pct}%. You can see and hear it in the same place.
station1.peakFar: Close. The loudest moment is around {pct}%. The picture is brightest there.
station1.peakExplain: Your browser measured this in the sound. Bright in the picture means loud.
station1.handoff: That is how I turn sound into words. Agent Echo will now look for a fake voice.

station2.name: Real or Fake?
station2.echoPrompt: Is this a human or a computer?
station2.prompt2: Case two. Listen for breaths, slips and hiss.
station2.prompt3: Case three. Check the gaps too.
station2.prompt4: Case four. This one is hard.
station2.specAlt: The sound picture for this case: time runs left to right, low tones at the bottom, high tones at the top.
station2.scoreHigh: Sharp listening. Now we test what compression does to the clues.
station2.scoreMid: Well done. Fake voices are hard to spot. Now add compression.
station2.scoreLow: This is hard. Fake voices keep improving. Now add compression.
station2.itWasReal: This voice was REAL. You heard a person.
station2.itWasFake: This voice was FAKE. A computer made it.
station2.fooledStat: {pct}% of visitors fell for this one too!
station2.realExplanation: Real. You can hear breaths and small slips. AI can create those details too.
station2.realExplanationB: Real. You can hear some room echo. A real recording can also sound perfectly clean.
station2.realExplanationC: Real. The voice wobbles, hesitates and breathes. Good fake voices do that too.
station2.clueCaveat: These are clues in this clip. New voice models also make breaths, hiss and room echo. A real clip can sound very clean.
station2.uncertainty: AI voices improve quickly. Compression erases many clues. The next stations lead to a check that always works.

station3.name: The compression machine
station3.echoIntro: The same sentence plays four times. Each version is compressed more. Watch the top of the picture.
station3.predictBody: The last setting is a really crackly voice message. Do you think Miko will still be able to write the sentence down?
station3.resultIdentical: Miko wrote down exactly the same sentence at the crackliest setting as at studio quality. The words survived the squashing completely.
station3.resultChanged: Miko wrote almost the same sentence at the crackliest setting. Most words survived. The details disappeared.
station3.resultSilent: At the crackliest setting Miko got nothing at all. Even the words were squashed away.
station3.echoAfter: The words come through. The high details disappear first. Compression makes a fake voice even harder to spot.
station3.tryAll: Listen to all four settings first
station3.specAlt: The sound picture at the {level} setting.
station3.mikoHearsNothing: …almost nothing any more. The sound is too squashed!

station4.name: The fake-voice factory
station4.pickSentence: What should the fake voice say? Pick a sentence.
station4.mikoHeard: Miko is listening to the message
station4.mikoVerdict: Sounds fine to me! Message received.
station4.lesson: Miko understood every word. The source stayed unclear. That is the problem with audio.
station4.scamTip: Real scammers do this too: they call parents with a fake voice of their child. Not sure? Hang up and call back on the number you already have.

final.intro: One last mission. This one matters outside the room.
final.title: A voice you know asks for money
final.body: It is late. A familiar voice asks for money in a voice message. It is urgent and meant to stay secret.
final.question: What do you do?

option.send: Send the money straight away. I recognise the voice.
option.reply: Reply to that same message and ask something only they would know.
option.callback: Call the number you already have saved, and ask them yourself.
option.unsure: I am not sure what to do.

why.send: A few seconds of audio can be enough to copy a voice. Voice recognition gives too little certainty for a payment.
why.reply: You would stay in the same conversation with the same sender. Choose another channel to reach the person yourself.
why.callback: Exactly. Call the number already saved in your phone. You reach the real person, even when the fake voice is perfect.
why.unsure: Doubt is enough reason to pause. Call the person on the number already saved in your phone.

final.takeaway: Stop. Choose another channel. Call back on a trusted number.

station5.name: Clone your own voice
station5.title: Your voice, new words
station5.privacy: Your recording stays on this computer and is deleted after this mission.
station5.readText: Today I am testing how a computer can copy my voice. I am speaking clearly, at my normal pace, with my usual rhythm and sound.
station5.review: This is your real recording. Ready to turn it into a new sentence?
station5.cloning: The local AI is building your voice
station5.wait: This can take several minutes on a computer without GPU acceleration.
station5.cloneText: This sounds like your voice. You never said this sentence.
station5.echoGuess: My model guess: {label}. Reliability of this guess: {confidence}.
station5.echoUnsure: I could not judge this recording reliably.
station5.lesson: Ten seconds was enough to create new words in your voice. A familiar voice is not proof of who is speaking.
station5.unavailable: The local voice models could not start. Continue and ask the facilitator to check the local model service.
station5.error: Cloning failed. Your recording was deleted. You can try again or continue.

station6.name: Detective Diploma
station6.title: Detective Diploma
station6.hardest: The hardest case fooled {pct}% of everyone!
station6.verifyCrowd: {pct}% chose to call back and check.
station6.echoOutro: AI changes how we make, share and trust voices. You can already do this today:
station6.tip1: Does a familiar voice ask for money or a secret? Hang up and call back on the number you already have. That works even when the fake is perfect.
station6.tip2: Breath, hiss and small mistakes can help. Apps and phones remove these details.
station6.tip3: Anyone can be fooled. Checking takes one phone call.

clue.tier1: This voice sounds very smooth. The box shows little wobble. New fake voices can wobble too.
clue.tier2: The box shows a bare gap between the words. A clean real recording can look the same.
clue.tier3: Almost real! But the stripes in the box run very straight and even. That's a clue in this one. A straight stripe on its own never decides it.
clue.tier4: Look at the gap between the words. A quiet room can create the same pattern in a real recording.
clue.tier5: This picture is very clean and even. That is a weak clue. My analysis ends around here.
clue.smoothHarmonics: The lines look smooth and even. A human voice often wobbles a little more. Treat this as a hint.
clue.noBreath: The voice starts without an audible breath. Real clips are sometimes trimmed just as tightly.
clue.hfCutoff: The high sound at the top stops suddenly. Some fake voices and phone calls both show this.
clue.tooClean: You hear little mouth noise, hiss or room echo. A studio microphone can make a real clip sound just as clean.
